clue.text: Could men possibly like The Times' pages?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the preceding letters may be laid out differently

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wondering aside on whether men could be suited to the newspaper's pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper pages are printed in vertical text strips, so they are laid out in columns.

clue.text: Transparent sheet for animation, one in suspect scale

clue.text: See porky in undergarment? Extremely far from ugly

parts.note: a vest is a sleeveless undershirt

explanation.surface: Someone spots a plump figure in underwear and judges it not ugly at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Porky is British rhyming slang: pork pie means lie. A vest in Britain is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as far as possible from ugly means being the most beautiful, the superlative of lovely.

clue.text: Astonishing feat of vehicle moving up in race

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

clue.text: Cut up over politician on the French case

parts.note: to axe is to cut
MP, Member of Parliament
le is French for the

explanation.walkthrough: Over and on simply stack the pieces in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is a particular instance, illustrating something more general.

clue.text: Minister's aide's retreat about key company

CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.walkthrough: The second ’s stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained church officer who assists the priest or minister in services and pastoral work.

clue.text: Criminal chap for a bit of bovver?

explanation.walkthrough: Bovver is British slang (from bother) for rowdy trouble-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, typically a bandit of the American Wild West.

clue.text: Who may take characters (or letters) from Alberta via Toronto?

definitions.text: Who may take characters (or letters) from Alberta via Toronto?

indicators.note: taking characters from a phrase means lifting a run of its letters out unchanged

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A question about who carries mail between two Canadian places.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters plays both ways: the hidden letters, and post a pilot may fly across Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flying a mail plane from province to city would carry correspondence across Canada.

clue.text: Supervise setting poetry in Old English

indicators.note: setting one thing in another means placing it inside, as a jewel is set

parts.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: An editor oversees verse composed in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct the work of others.

clue.text: Those used to sea voyages following one existing stomach remedy

parts.note: one who lives, i.e. exists
old salts are experienced sailors

explanation.walkthrough: Liver here is read as one who lives, not the organ.

clue.text: Fish that is lacking tail

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is

explanation.walkthrough: Id est, abbreviated i.e., loses its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater carp-like species, and several of them are ides.

clue.text: Working police train son, having authority over him?

parts.note: the three words supply all fourteen letters

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means in the place of a parent, as a teacher or guardian acts towards a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a parent's stead, legally gives an adult responsibility and control over a child.

clue.text: Functions introducing eastern European school of painting's style

parts.note: sines are trigonometric functions

E is short for European

clue.text: One nursed by tireless flying doctor?

flying suggests letters scattered through the air, landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A patient is cared for by an indefatigable doctor who flies to rural areas.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a noun for the nurse's colleague, but it is the verb for neutering a pet.

clue.text: Gets on "soundly" without women in general

clue.text: To him, sins destroyed religious belief

parts.note: the three words supply the letters

clue.text: Issued blood without too much kept stored

parts.note: to bleed is to lose blood
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A wound bled without losing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking in the surface, but here it means outside, its older sense.

clue.text: Where one sees retired skater run for captain?

R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A former skater stands for the role of team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired skater suggests a sports star, but it is read as the skater's position: off the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army or navy, so a commissioned soldier or sailor.

clue.text: Fuss about station food in Mexico

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss
STA is the abbreviation for station

explanation.definitionFit: A tostado is a fried, crisp corn tortilla eaten in Mexican cooking, often topped.

clue.text: Stuffing cod, say, work with a bit of pasta like macaroni

parts.note: cod is an example of a fish
OP is short for opus, a work

parts.note: the first letter of pasta

explanation.walkthrough: Macaroni looks like the pasta but is an 18th-century word for an overdressed dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century macaroni was a vain dandy who affected continental fashions, so dandified.

clue.text: Pelt round after one so wildly

indicators.note: after places the ring-shaped letter later than the single letter

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Pelt looks like a verb meaning race, and round like an adverb; both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Furioso is an Italian musical direction telling the performer to play with furious energy.

clue.text: Cautiously introduce power — owns home without energy

indicators.note: without means outside, so the earlier words go around the last one

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

in means at home
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A householder brings in electricity gradually, having a home with no power.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase something in is to bring it into use gradually, stage by stage.

clue.text: Make rough speed north round outskirts of Slough

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

parts.note: the first and last letters of Slough

explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a commuter town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harshen is a verb meaning to make harsher, coarser or more severe.

clue.text: Is Israel concerned with splitting element for source of power?

taken as written

clue.text: Official record showing a court answer

parts.note: taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

clue.text: Poet mostly reserved about source of rhymes

clue.text: Boyfriend is guy Manon treated roughly
